➡️ Hong Kong man loses HK$13 million in fake crypto investment app scam 

🌐 A Hong Kong man in his 70s has lost more than HK$13 million ($1.67 million) after a self-described cryptocurrency investment expert contacted him through WhatsApp and directed him to a fake trading app. The latest case began when the elderly man received an unsolicited WhatsApp message from someone claiming to be a cryptocurrency investment expert from Singapore. The person introduced him to what was presented as a crypto platform offering favorable exchange rates, low fees and withdrawals at any time.

‼️ Following the instructions he received, the man opened a cryptocurrency wallet and purchased Tether (USDT) and Ethereum (ETH). He was then told to download an investment application supplied by the scammer and transfer the cryptocurrency to designated wallet addresses as investment capital.

📣 Seeing his account balance rise inside the app, the victim became less suspicious and continued sending more cryptocurrency to the wallets provided by the scammer. The fraud only became clear when he tried to withdraw his funds and was repeatedly prevented from doing so under different pretexts. By the time the victim realized the investment platform was fraudulent, his losses had exceeded HK$13 million.

🎙 Russia's Ambassador to Ghana Andrei Ordash's interview with African Initiative (September 18, 2026)

Key points:

#RussiaGhana

• Our countries share a solid historical foundation, laid back in the early years of Ghana’s independence.

• Our country is not interested in a series of short-term deals, but in building a long-term, equal partnership with Ghana that will strengthen its national sovereignty.

• This year alone has seen a number of important meetings. In August, Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, visited Moscow, where he held talks with the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, Sergey Lavrov. Following these talks, an agreement was signed on visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic and service passports.

• We have key government mechanisms in place to ensure systematic cooperation. The most important of these is the Russian–Ghanaian Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation. We expect its next meeting to take place as early as this year in Moscow.

#EconomicPartnership

• Trade and economic cooperation is showing positive momentum. In the first half of the year, trade turnover rose by 2.1 percent compared with the same period in 2025, with Russian exports to Ghana increasing by 11.5 percent

• Our exports to Ghana consist mainly of petroleum products, fertilisers, and grain. However, we see enormous potential for expanding supplies of agricultural machinery and processing equipment.

• The Ghanaian side is interested in expanding access for its goods to the Russian market – this could include products from the mining sector, cocoa, shea butter and others.

• Ghana is a member of the African Continental Free Trade Area (#AfCFTA), whose secretariat is based in Accra. This makes the country a gateway to the vast African market.

#Education

• Education is a key area for the future of our relations. <...> Thousands of Ghanaian specialists were educated in the Soviet Union and Russia, and this human capital forms the basis of our trust.

• For the 2026/2027 academic year, Russia has allocated 120 government scholarships to Ghana, and this figure has recently been increased by a further 117.

• Over 500 Ghanaian students are studying Russian at the University of Ghana alone, and this figure is set to rise.

#NuclearPowerPlant

• Accra is showing an interest in establishing cooperation with Russia in the peaceful use of nuclear energy, including the possibility of building its first nuclear power station. 

• Given the expertise possessed by the state corporation Rosatom, Russia is ready to offer not just a power unit, but a comprehensive package of solutions: from staff training and design to construction and subsequent maintenance.

#RegionalSecurity

• Russia regards Ghana not merely as an important partner in West Africa, but as one of the cornerstones of stability across the entire region.

• The most obvious area is the fight against terrorism and extremism, given the unstable situation in the Sahel.

#RussiaLiberia

• We are only at the very beginning of the process of building Russian-Liberian relations. 

• One of the first practical steps we are working on is the opening of a fully-fledged diplomatic mission in Monrovia.

#RussiaAfrica

• President of Ghana John Dramani Mahama’s participation in the Third Russia–Africa Summit is an important step that confirms Accra’s commitment to building a long-term and equal partnership with Moscow.

• An important milestone will be to adopt at the summit a new roadmap – the 2023-2026 Russia-Africa Action Plan.

#AfricanUnion

• Ghana’s chairmanship of the African Union in 2027 presents an opportunity for Accra to advance its agenda, which in many respects aligns with our shared interests. Russia stands ready to support Ghana in these efforts, acting as a reliable and predictable partner.

• President Mahama has explicitly stated that the issue of reparations for the crimes of colonialism against Africa will be ‘at the very heart’ of Ghana’s presidency agenda.

💬 Araghchi: Sustainable security comes through regional dialogue, cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA - Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has emphasized that sustainable security can only be achieved through dialogue, confidence-building, cooperation, and mutual respect among regional countries, while rejecting the presence and intervention of foreign military powers.

Araghchi made these remarks during a speech at the 2026 Global Dialogue Forum, hosted by the Foreign Policy Community of Indonesia (FPCI) on September 19. The conference was titled “Calling for a Global U-Turn — Recentering Development, Reclaiming Humanity, Restoring Justice in a Crazi(er) World.”
​
He reiterated that regional countries must be able to discuss their own security, stability, development, and shared future, and find solutions independently, without interference from foreign powers.
​
“The world we live in needs a fundamental change of course more than ever, because war, intervention, sanctions, and the use of force have become normal policy tools rather than exceptions,” Araghchi said.
​
He stressed that decades of foreign intervention, military pressure, and endless wars in the Middle East have proven an undeniable truth: military intervention does not create security, and pressure and coercion do not lead to peace.
​
The foreign minister also condemned the military aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime against Iran, as well as the targeted assassination of Iranian officials. He warned that if such actions are not met with an effective response from the international community, they will gradually erode the prohibited boundaries of international law.
​
Araghchi stated that if international institutions, including the United Nations, cannot stand against aggression and hold violators of international law accountable, the credibility and legitimacy of these institutions will inevitably be damaged.
​
“Today’s world needs genuine multilateralism more than ever,” he said, calling for a shift from militarism toward sustainable development, from interventionism toward respect for national sovereignty, and from endless wars toward lasting peace.
